transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-12
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (DataQube CTO), Sophie Tran (ML Engineer), Evan Rocha (Infra), Lara (SRE)
---
Summary: Short scoping call to align on POC success criteria for benchmarking, workload sizing, benchmark harness integration, and a plan for streaming vs non-streaming tests. Agreed to share harness and run an integration lab next week.
Topics: success criteria, workload profile, sample prompts, load testing tools, streaming vs non-streaming behavior, infra requirements, timelines
---
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I think we have the usual suspects, Marcus, Sophie, Evan, can you hear us?
00:12 Marcus (DataQube): Yeah loud and clear, thanks Alex. We got a fairly packed agenda, mostly around the POC bench plan.
00:20 Priya (Redwood SE): Cool, we'll focus on success criteria, what you want to push in terms of RPS and concurrency, and how your existing scripts can plug into our harness.
00:33 Sophie (DataQube): Awesome. To set expectation, our main goal is to validate latency SLOs at 95th and throughput cost tradeoffs. We have both streaming and batch generation use cases.
00:45 Alex: Perfect, that's inline with other POCs. Marcus, can you quickly say who the stakeholders are and the timeline?
00:52 Marcus: CTO + infra + our ML platform team. Stakeholders want a 3-week POC: week 1 integration, week 2 runs & tuning, week 3 final benchmarks + report. Can you hit that?
01:05 Alex: We can, yes — assuming we get your canonical prompts and traffic profile this week. We'll also need a small dedicated quota for predictable capacity.
01:16 Evan (Infra): For the dedicated side we'll need to know whether the harness will originate from our VPC or from Redwood-hosted runners. I think we prefer VPC for data residency.
01:28 Priya: Noted. We support both—our private harness can run in a customer VPC via a runner, but there are egress and peering considerations. We'll include a network checklist.
01:40 Sophie: Quick Q: streaming vs non-streaming, how do you benchmark those differently?
01:45 Priya: Good question. For streaming we measure end-to-end time to first token and token sustain rate; non-streaming is full-response latency. Our harness supports both modes: you can replay your streaming websocket-like script or do batched HTTP calls.
02:00 Speaker 1: uh mm one more thing on streaming, sometimes transcriptions call it "streamed callbacks" — been mis-labeled in our docs, we'll correct.
02:12 Alex: We'll share two sample runner scripts: a streaming k6 script and a non-streaming locust example. Both are in the repo we'll send.
02:21 Marcus: For success criteria — we care about 95p latency < 400ms for short prompts (<256 tokens), cost per 1M tokens, and model fidelity compared to our existing hosted provider. Also reliability during 1h soak.
02:38 Priya: Great, can you quantify RPS or concurrency? That informs batching and warm KV cache policies.
02:44 Sophie: Typical peak is 80 RPS for short interactive flows, but some scheduled jobs batch 50 requests every minute. Long-form generation is lower QPS but higher tokens per request.
02:58 Alex: That's helpful. For benchmarking we'll recommend a mix: steady-state 80 RPS short prompt test, burst test to 200 concurrent connections for 2 minutes, and a long-form throughput run at 10 RPS with 2k token responses.
03:15 Evan: For the Dedicated trial, what's the recommended GPU footprint? We want to mirror production-ish behavior.
03:22 Priya: For initial tests we usually provision 2 x A10/GPU-ish nodes (or equivalent g4/g5 family) to let us see batching effects; if you use quantized variants that changes CPU vs GPU memory needs. We'll add guidance.
03:37 Sophie: Any caveats on model variants? We may want to test a smaller quantized variant for cost comparisons.
03:43 Priya: Absolutely — we'll include a recommended matrix: base-large (fp16), quantized-8, and a faster small model. The harness will auto-switch between variants for regression tests.
03:58 Alex: On telemetry, we need token-level metrics and per-route latency. Sophie, can you mark which endpoints are high-priority?
04:06 Sophie: Yes I will. I'll flag 12 routes as high-priority, mostly interactive chat endpoints.
04:14 Speaker 2: (background) note, our SOC2 team asked about audit logs during POC — they want immutable logs.
04:20 Alex: Good call — Redwood can keep verbose audit logs and we can provide limited retention copies for the trial. We'll send the security addendum.
04:32 Marcus: Also curious about evaluation harness integration: our existing scripts are in Python and use requests with websockets for streaming. How hard is plug-and-play?
04:42 Priya: Usually straightforward. We'll provide a small shim that adapts your websocket callbacks to our harness API. If you can give us one or two representative scripts we can convert them during the lab.
04:54 Sophie: We have about 5000 prompts in our canonical set — some are labeled latency-sensitive. We'll export a random 10% sample for initial runs.
05:03 Alex: That's perfect. For throughput tests we prefer the full histogram so we can model realistic inter-arrival times.
05:12 Priya: Regarding load generation, do you have a preference for tools? We support k6, locust, and a lightweight Go-based runner for high-concurrency streaming tests.
05:24 Evan: We currently use locust for HTTP and a custom node.js script for streaming. Might be easiest to keep that and wrap it into Redwood harness.
05:33 Priya: Good — we'll provide examples to wrap node.js streaming into our runner. Expect some fiddly bits around websocket ping/pong and backpressure.
05:45 Sophie: How do you measure token billing during bench vs real billing? We want cost estimates to be realistic.
05:52 Alex: For the POC we'll capture token counts and apply your expected pricing to give an apples-to-apples cost per 1M tokens. We'll also show the effect of batching and caching.
06:05 Speaker 1: small transcription note: 'KV cache' sometimes comes out as 'K-V cash' in older transcripts lol.
06:12 Priya: Ha, yes. We'll explain prefix/KV caching and how warm state impacts first request latency. For soak tests we recommend a warm-up phase to prime caches.
06:24 Marcus: About metrics — we'll need p50/p95/p99, error rates, throughput, and cost. Also per-model memory/CPU pressure logs.
06:34 Alex: We'll include those in the benchmark report template. Priya, can you outline the runbook?
06:40 Priya: Sure. High-level: 1) integrate scripts into harness and validate in a small-scale smoke test; 2) run warm-up with increasing load to prime KV cache; 3) run steady-state and burst profiles; 4) run long-form generation; 5) capture telemetry and compare across model variants; 6) produce a report with recommendations. We'll attach the checklist.
07:03 Sophie: Timeline-wise your earlier 3-week plan works if we get artifacts early. Can Redwood commit to the lab session next week?
07:11 Alex: Yes, we can do a 90-min lab on 2025-03-20 — Priya, you're good?
07:16 Priya: Yep, I'll reserve time. We'll need Evan to set up VPC runner access or allow Redwood-hosted runner for initial smoke.
07:25 Evan: I'll check peering and security approvals — might be faster to do Redwood-hosted for the first smoke test then move to VPC.
07:34 Marcus: That sounds pragmatic. One more thing: model fidelity — we will run a small eval set to compare outputs against current provider; we need deterministic seeds if possible.
07:46 Priya: We'll include an eval harness that captures outputs and supports simple diffs and quality metrics. Deterministic seeds vary by model but we'll attempt to standardize where supported.
07:58 Alex: Competitor check — any existing contracts with Anthropic or others we should be aware of?
08:03 Marcus: We have an active contract with a major hosted provider but no long-term commit. This POC is to evaluate cost and reliability.
08:12 Sophie: Also note regulatory constraint — some data cannot leave EU region. We'll mark those prompts and plan region-specific runs.
08:21 Priya: Good, we'll include region pinning in the runbook.
08:28 Speaker 3: small pause, there's some background chatter, sorry.
08:35 Alex: No worries. Moving to integration specifics — Alex: action items recap: we'll send repo + runbook; Priya: prepare harness configs; Sophie: share prompts and traffic histogram; Evan: network checks.
08:52 Marcus: Sounds good. On metrics export — do you support Prometheus scraping?
08:57 Priya: Yes, we expose Prometheus metrics + structured JSON outputs and a CSV summary. We'll provide Grafana dashboard JSON for quick import.
09:10 Sophie: For the final report, can you include cost breakdown per 1M tokens and expected monthly cost at current traffic?
09:17 Alex: Yes we'll include a cost model spreadsheet.
09:20 Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
09:25 Priya: Anything else on blockers?
09:29 Marcus: Only the SOC2/RBAC thing — once you send the security addendum we'll route to our compliance folks.
09:36 Alex: We'll send that with the harness package.
09:40 Sophie: Great. One operational question: during soak tests what's the best way to simulate KV cache cold start?
09:46 Priya: Start with a cold run then run a warm-up with similar prompt distribution for 30 minutes to a few hours depending on dataset; we can script that into the harness.
09:56 Evan: For network, we'll need to ensure no unexpected throttling on our side; I'll coordinate with SRE.
10:03 Alex: Ok, let's close with next steps and owners — repeat the 4 items we put in next_steps.
10:12 Marcus: Good. Thanks everyone, looking forward to lab next week.
10:18 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the repo and calendar invite. Bye.
---
Post-call notes:
- Agreed to 3-week POC timeline contingent on artifacts delivered.
- Key success criteria: 95p latency < 400ms for short prompts, cost per 1M tokens targeting 20-30% reduction vs incumbent, reliability during 1h soak
- Bench matrix: steady-state short prompt (80 RPS), burst to 200 concurrent, long-form 10 RPS 2k tokens, cross-variant comparison (fp16 / q8 / small-fast)
- Integration path: customer node.js streaming scripts + locust HTTP -> Redwood harness via shim.
- Security checklist: audit logs, SSO, VPC runner considerations noted.
